subject: Concurrency sizing & quota check-in — Umbrella Payments pilot
messages:
From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@umbrellapay.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@umbrellapay.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T15:02:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: realtime checkout UX / concurrency needs

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the PoC: 

- Business KPI: reduce checkout latency to improve conversion for flagged merchants. We expect a sustained workload of ~2,500 inference requests/minute during peak windows, with a baseline of ~600 rpm outside peaks.
- Concurrency: our frontend will open long-lived streaming connections for token-level updates (websocket/SSE). We need to support ~400 simultaneous streaming sessions at baseline and tolerate bursts up to ~1,200 concurrent sessions for marketing surges (bursts typically last ~20–40s).
- Latency targets: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 250ms (we understand p50 will be lower); streaming partials should be surfaced within < 60ms of token generation for good UX.
- Throughput: average payload per request ~180 tokens; we plan batching on the client where possible but need strict SLOs for interactive paths.

Questions for Redwood:
1) How does your connection pooling interact with streaming websockets? Can a single connection service multiple concurrent streams (multiplexing) or do we need 1 socket per session?
2) What are your default concurrency/rate limits for hosted accounts? Is there a short-term increase process for PoC bursts?
3) How do per-route quotas and backpressure signals work — can the service return a graceful 429 with retry-after that supports our client backoff?

I've attached our short PoC requirements doc (umpay_poc_requirements.pdf) and a simple event flow PNG.

Appreciate the suggestions you mentioned on the call for pilot sizing — happy to align next steps and get a technical deep-dive on the streaming path.

Best,
Sara
Sara Jensen
Head of Product, Umbrella Payments
~  
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@umbrellapay.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@umbrellapay.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T19:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: realtime checkout UX / concurrency needs

Sara — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment, that helps a lot. Below is a concise answer to each question plus a proposed pilot configuration so procurement and engineering can align quickly.

1) Connection pooling & streaming
- Default hosted model: websockets/SSE are treated as long-lived front-door connections. We do not multiplex multiple logical user sessions over a single websocket for security/traceability reasons in hosted plans — 1 session = 1 socket. For Dedicated/private we offer multiplexing via our connection proxy to save socket counts; that requires a small network policy and config change.

2) Default limits and short-term increases
- Hosted defaults: 250 concurrent connections and 1,000 concurrent requests (logical in-flight requests) per account as a safe starting point.
- Pilot flexibility: we can provision a time-bounded increase for your PoC to support the burst profile you described. For Umbrella Payments I propose the following pilot quota set (subject to signed PoC agreement):
  * Baseline concurrent streaming sessions: 600
  * Sustained concurrent in-flight requests: 800
  * Burst allowance (30s windows): up to 1,500 concurrent sessions for max 60s per hour
  * Per-route rate limit: configurable (we can tag interactive routes and give priority)

3) Backpressure and 429 handling
- We return standard 429s with a Retry-After header and a JSON payload with an error_code you can use to implement backoff. For streaming endpoints we offer a graceful pre-close message indicating a soft-throttle so the client can reconnect to a fallback route.

Cost model note: pricing is still per-token for generation + per-minute connection surcharge for long-lived sockets on hosted. For the pilot we will cap incremental socket fees (proposal attached: redwood_pilot_proposal.pdf). Dedicated reservations move to a flat monthly capacity model which eliminates per-socket surcharges.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Technical deep-dive (30–45m) with your infra and our serving engineers (I’ve CCed Karthik). Options: Wed 2027-05-26 or Thu 2027-05-27.
- Sign PoC MSA addendum and PO to enable the temporary quota increase.
- We’ll stage a short smoke test (10–15m) to validate concurrent session behavior before any marketing-driven burst.

I’ll leave the technical details to Karthik for the deep-dive, but happy to handle procurement syncs.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@umbrellapay.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@umbrellapay.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:33:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: realtime checkout UX / concurrency needs

Vanessa / Sara — thanks, good clarity. A couple of follow-ups from the engineering side before the deep-dive: 

- Token streaming + connection pool: if 1 socket = 1 session on hosted, that drives a lot of sockets. Can you confirm whether your hosted socket surcharge applies per TCP connection or per authenticated session token? We sometimes multiplex auth contexts at the proxy layer and could adapt if that helps.
- KV cache and session locality: we plan to use short-lived session-specific state (few KBs per session) for reranking personalization. Does your runtime evict KV cache aggressively when concurrency spikes? Do we need sticky routing to avoid cold-cache penalties?
- Retry semantics: If an interactive request gets 429 under burst, will the Retry-After be accurate enough for client to circuit-break or should we implement a separate local queue?

Attaching a quick proto_event_flow.png for reference. If you can confirm the hosted socket billing and caching behavior it will help us size the PoC infra.

Thanks — Marco
Senior Infra Engineer, Umbrella Payments
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@umbrellapay.com>, Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@umbrellapay.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T10:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: realtime checkout UX / concurrency needs

Marco — great questions, answered inline here. Karthik will cover the deep technical details in the session but this should unblock sizing and procurement.

- Hosted socket billing: hosted accounts are billed per authenticated long-lived socket session (per websocket). If you authenticate multiple logical sessions over one physical connection we charge per authenticated session token — the short version is "per session". For the PoC we can waive incremental socket charges for the pilot cohort; the redwood_pilot_proposal.pdf attached spells that out.

- KV cache & session locality: our serving runtime uses a sharded KV cache keyed by model + session id. Under heavy contention we do soft-evictions (LRU within a shard) which can create cold-cache penalties; we offer sticky routing on Dedicated and Private deployments to maintain hot-cache locality. For hosted PoC we will reserve a warm-up window and knob the cache retention to reduce eviction risk during your expected bursts.

- Retry semantics & 429 behavior: Retry-After is reliable for the short burst windows we provision. For critical interactive paths we recommend a hybrid: client-side local queue + immediate reconnect to a lower-cost fallback endpoint (we can host a tiny ephemeral fallback that uses more aggressive batching but slower token pacing). We can provide a sample client snippet that implements the recommended backoff and fallback pattern.

Scheduling: Karthik — can you take Wed 2027-05-26 16:00 UTC or Thu 2027-05-27 15:00 UTC for a technical deep-dive? Please confirm and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Next big-ticket items for Umbrella to action:
- Sign PoC addendum (I’ll loop legal once you confirm)
- Provide a short list of your interactive endpoints we should tag for priority routing (JSON or sheet)
- Confirm whether you prefer Hosted pilot (fast, per-socket billing) or Dedicated pilot (flat capacity, better locality).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
